appliesTo: the leading text part of the certified scan-identify provider request
note: The certified prompt is never rewritten. This text is appended after it, so the certified instructions remain first, verbatim and traceable. Lines are joined with a single newline; the joined text is what textSha256 covers.
designConstraint: Overlay LENGTH is a measured variable in this candidate, not an incidental property. The certified request already consumes a mean 1,698 prompt tokens, and output plus thinking share one 2,048-token ceiling. The rejected phase2a-v1.0.0 overlay added roughly 1,000 prompt tokens and moved the count of cases finishing within 20 tokens of that ceiling from 6 to 13, with invalid output rising 18.2% to 42.4%. This overlay is held to roughly a fifth of that length (about 192 tokens against about 999) so the specificity instruction can be tested without re-running the length confound. At the observed sensitivity of roughly one extra invalid case per 125 added prompt tokens, this overlay predicts about 1.5 extra invalid cases on the 33-case development split, against the 8 the rejected overlay produced.
lines: K SCAN AI PHASE 6 CANDIDATE INSTRUCTIONS (phase6-scanner-v1.0-a)
Everything above still applies. Two refinements. No new fields, no renamed
fields, no change to the response shape.
Use the specific fashion term the image supports: "trench coat" rather than
"coat", "chelsea boot" rather than "shoe", "tote bag" rather than "bag". Do
not answer with a generic word such as "clothing", "item", "apparel" or
"accessory" when a specific term is actually visible.
Read the image and answer at once. Do not deliberate, weigh alternatives, or
reason step by step before writing. Where a detail is not visible, give the
value this contract already defines for an absent detail and move on rather
